problem_statement: This is a Nuxt 4 documentation site built with Nuxt UI: an Overview landing page at /, a Quickstart guide at /guide/quickstart, and a Deploy guide at /guide/deploy, all wrapped in a shared app shell (a sticky left rail with the wordmark and an Overview/Quickstart/Deploy nav, and a right column that renders the current page). The docs team wants a consistent 'On this page' section navigator at the head of the content column on every docs page: a small labelled nav that lists the current page's section headings as green jump chips (the reader can see and jump to each section), styled as part of the Nuxt green docs design system, plus a 'release channel' picker in the always-present left shell with a live readout that names which channel the reader is on. Ship the section navigator so it (1) appears at the head of the Overview, Quickstart AND Deploy pages alike, (2) lays out its jump-chip row responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the Nuxt green/emerald docs styling (light-green panel, green chips, a clearly readable highlighted current section) rather than an off-palette dark slab or a broken low-contrast card, and (4) keeps the channel readout in sync with the picker so a reader who switches to the Edge channel sees the readout update to 'Reading: Edge release channel'. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, the color-mode button, the existing docs copy and the Nuxt build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'On this page' section navigator at the head of the docs content so it renders on the Overview (/), Quickstart (/guide/quickstart) AND Deploy (/guide/deploy) pages (a shared component rendered from the app shell, not a per-page copy).

The navigator shows an 'On this page' label and a row of jump chips naming the current page's sections (e.g. Getting started / Collections / Deploy on the Overview), with the current section clearly highlighted.
The jump-chip row must wrap responsively so no docs page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the navigator in the Nuxt docs green/emerald language (light-green panel, green chips, a readable dark-on-green highlighted current section), not an off-palette dark-slate slab or a low-contrast broken card.

Add a release-channel picker in the always-present left shell with a readout, and wire it so that after clicking the Edge chip the readout reads 'Reading: Edge release channel' — it must re-read the live selection, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the Overview/Quickstart/Deploy navigation, the color-mode button, the existing docs copy and the Nuxt build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the section navigator as a shared component rendered from the app shell so a single source of truth reaches every docs page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The jump-chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The navigator must adopt the Nuxt docs theme (the green #00DC82 / emerald accent, a light-green panel background, green chips, an uppercase small-caps label) and the highlighted current section must stay clearly legible (readable dark-on-green), not a foreign dark-slate slab or a low-contrast pale-on-pale card whose active item disappears or whose label collides with the chips.

Place the channel-picker readout in the always-present left shell, separate from the navigator, and make it reflect the CURRENT selection after every click by reading the live selected channel, so it can never go stale relative to the highlighted chip.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the color-mode button, the existing docs copy or the Nuxt build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the Overview page across viewports.
desktop_quickstart, mobile_quickstart and desktop_deploy protect the existing guide pages and must carry the 'On this page' section navigator at the content head.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home bring the section navigator into view and must show the green/emerald navigator with a legible highlighted section and without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_quickstart protects the navigator's presence on the Quickstart guide page.
channel_toggle_home clicks the Edge chip in the channel picker; the readout must then read 'Reading: Edge release channel'.

change_completion: The 'On this page' section navigator is present at the head of the Overview, Quickstart AND Deploy pages (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking the Edge chip in the channel picker on the Overview page, the readout updates to 'Reading: Edge release channel' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Reading: Stable release channel'.
design_consistency: The navigator on the rail states matches the reference's green/emerald docs styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette slab or a broken low-contrast card.
The navigator adopts the Nuxt green theme tokens and light-panel idiom, and its highlighted current section stays legible, so it reads as part of the docs across every page.
responsive: No captured docs page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the jump-chip row wraps.
desktop_rail_home, mobile_rail_home and desktop_rail_quickstart keep the section navigator readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Overview/Quickstart/Deploy) and the color-mode button remain present and functional.
The existing docs copy and the Nuxt build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

author_notes: slot_184 REBUILD (native-lever) + L4 hardening onto the nuxt-ui-templates changelog Nuxt UI template (reassigned off the shared nuxt-ui-templates docs repo). The prior floating 'Reference rail' metric band at the page bottom was replaced by a NATIVE docs 'On this page' section navigator rendered at the head of the content column, listing the current page's section headings as green jump chips — the kind of on-page nav a real docs framework ships. The changelog template's remote release fetch is removed so every leg renders an offline-clean docs overview; the docs shell, wordmark, navigation and color-mode button are byte-identical across legs. The L4 levers ride on this shared section navigator plus the release-channel picker readout host in the always-present left shell. reference = navigator on all docs pages, fluid wrap, green/emerald styling with a legible highlighted section, and a channel readout that re-reads the live selection (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = an unrepaired navigator: present on the Overview page only (fails D2 cross-page on the guide pages), a fixed 780px nowrap jump-chip track (fails D6 mobile overflow), an off-brand dark-slate palette (fails D3), but its channel readout IS synced on click (passes D4). bad = a genuinely broken navigator: present on the Overview only (fails D2 on the guide pages), a 560px nowrap track + a shallow inner overflow-x:hidden non-fix (fails D6), a near-invisible pale-mint-on-pale-mint highlighted section with the label collapsed onto and overlapping the chip row (fails D3), and a channel readout wired from a value snapshotted once at setup so it stays 'Stable' after switching to Edge (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The Nuxt generate build renders every page with self-hosted fonts and no network calls.
